sentences.text: Petitioner has field this writ petition under Article 226 of Constitution of India making a prayer to quash proceedings of land acquisition.
2 . It is submitted by learned counsel for petitioner that notices were issued to petitioner about 40 years back and, thereafter, no compensation has been paid and land has been acquired.
It is submitted that as per Section 24(2) of Land Acquisition and Rehabilitation Act, 2013, land acquisition proceeding has lapsed.
On going through the petition, it is found that petitioner has not given any specific dates, when notifications were issued and when award was passed.
It was also not mentioned that as to what amount of compensation is to be paid to petitioner.
Petitioner has filed a generalized petition without making any averments in it.
5. Considering aforesaid circumstances, petition is dismissed.
6 . Petitioner is at liberty to file proper writ petition mentioning proper particulars in the writ petition regarding notification, passing of award and acquisition of land by respondents.

(VISHAL DHAGAT) JUDGE nd Smt Sheela Dahiya vs The State Of M.P. on 17 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/41436012/
